items.statement: Strand A will show that audit and feedback reduces antimicrobial use mainly where recommendations are delivered in person, with few reports from surgery, intensive care or hospitals under 200 beds.
items.rationale: Consistent with the retrieved surgical and caseload evidence (claims c2, c5).
items.risks: Measures too heterogeneous to show a pattern.

items.statement: Strand B will show that timing, a named senior recipient and a trusted in-team pharmacist are the main reasons recommendations are accepted, across surgery and intensive care.
items.rationale: Consistent with claims c3 and c4.
items.risks: Few studies outside large teaching hospitals.

items.statement: Both strands will say little about small hospitals, where telephone advice is the norm.
items.rationale: Small hospitals are rare in the retrieved records.
items.risks: French-language reports may change the picture.

summary: Three mapping expectations, one per strand and one on small hospitals; h1 selected to organise strand A, with h2 kept for strand B.
